name: Shammua
overview: Shammua was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as a son of David. His presence in Scripture is brief and primarily noted through his lineage, emphasizing his place within the royal family of Israel. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shammua likely means '[YHWH] hears' or 'rumor,' reflecting a Hebrew origin tied to divine hearing. An alternate form of his name, Shimea, means 'he has heard' or 'obedient one,' both names underscoring themes of hearing and responsiveness. Neither name is indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Shammua is explicitly recorded as a son of David, the king of Israel, and also as a son of Bathsheba, David's wife. These relationships firmly place him within the central royal household of Israel's history.
scriptureSignificance: Shammua's significance lies in his inclusion among David's sons, highlighting the continuation of David's lineage, which is foundational for biblical history and messianic anticipation. Although little else is recorded about his personal deeds or character, his identity as a son of David and Bathsheba connects him to the covenantal promises made to David's house. His mention contributes to the genealogical framework that undergirds the biblical narrative of God's redemptive plan through David's line.
